title: When Galaxies Collide
objective: After this level you can explain galaxy collisions and the future merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda.
summary: Galaxies merge over hundreds of millions of years. Andromeda is heading our way, but stars almost never hit each other.

cards.headline: Andromeda is on a collision course with the Milky Way.
Cosmic collisions
cards.body: Galaxies can collide and merge, pulling each other into new shapes over hundreds of millions of years. Andromeda, about 2.5 million light-years away, is moving toward the Milky Way, and the two are expected to merge in about 4.5 billion years.

cards.headline: Crash without a crash
cards.body: When galaxies collide, individual stars almost never hit each other. The spaces between stars are so vast that the galaxies pass through each other, their gravity reshaping both. Mergers like this are one way galaxies grow.

cards.fact: You can see the other half of this collision.
cards.context: From a dark site, Andromeda is visible to the naked eye as a faint smudge, about 2.5 million light-years away and slowly getting closer.

cards.headline: Galaxy collisions: forecast

options.label: They are swallowed by black holes

questions.explanation: The spaces between stars are so vast that stars almost never collide, even when whole galaxies merge.

questions.prompt: From Level 10: Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away. Roughly how long until the merger?

options.label: About 2.5 million years
options.rationale: That’s the light travel time, not the merger.

options.label: About 13.8 billion years
options.rationale: That’s the age of the universe.

questions.explanation: Andromeda is 2.5 million light-years away but moving slowly by cosmic standards: the merger is expected in about 4.5 billion years.
